children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

recently_moved_to_uk.description: Whether the claimant has recently moved to the UK.

right_to_reside_status.description: A plain English description of the claimant's right-to-reside position.

I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children for whom you'd like to claim Child Benefit? If yes, could you tell me their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 3 years old and lives with me here at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have Alex who is 3 years old and lives with you at home.

To assess your eligibility, I need to ask: Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK. Though I should mention that I've only recently moved here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you've recently moved to the UK, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

What is your immigration or residency status in the UK? For example, are you:
- A British citizen
- An EU/EEA/Swiss national with settled or pre-settled status
- Someone with another type of visa or right to reside
- Or another status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not really sure about all the technical terms to be honest. I've moved here recently but I'm not certain about my exact right-to-reside status or how it all works.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's completely understandable - the terminology can be confusing. Let me ask this a different way to help clarify.

Where did you move to the UK from, and do you know if you have any official permission or documentation that allows you to live in the UK? For example, do you have a visa, a residence permit, citizenship, or any other official status that allows you to be here?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not go into all those details right now. I'm just trying to find out if I can claim Child Benefit for Alex. Is there a way to check my eligibility without getting into all the specifics of my immigration status? I'm not really sure about those details myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

I understand you'd prefer not to go into those details, and I appreciate your situation. However, I do need to be honest with you about the requirements.

To determine eligibility for Child Benefit, one of the key criteria is that you must live in the UK **and** have the right to reside here. The rules are quite specific about residency and immigration status, and they vary depending on your circumstances.

Without knowing whether you have the right to reside in the UK, I cannot definitively determine whether you would be eligible for Child Benefit, even though Alex is under 16 and lives with you (which would normally meet the basic requirements).

Since you're uncertain about your right to reside status, I would recommend:
- Checking any documentation you received when you moved to the UK
- Or contacting the Child Benefit Office directly, who can help you understand your specific situation

Given that you don't have sufficient information about your right to reside status, and this is a crucial factor in determining eligibility, I'll need to provide an assessment based on the information available.

Would you like me to proceed with making that assessment now?

conversation.text: Yes, please go ahead and give me your assessment based on what I've told you. I understand you need to know about the right to reside, but I just don't have that information right now.
